title: Scrapbook: Audubon tea room, first Red Hot groups and jazz club photos
summary: Photos of his first bands under his own name, recordings, a jazz club broadcast and advertising slogan.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Didn't Greenwood take one of them pictures of both of them?
No, that would be Bernie Stunner who was a doctor then.
Because that was an Audubon tea room.
I think that's one of the first jobs I've booked over here on your left, Dick.
Yeah, and Audubon tea room Al Lowberry on bass, who I hardly remember. Oh yeah, and I see the first group you played with under the title of Red Hot Castillo? What's his name?
Yeah, he played at the lake, you know, for the girl boys mostly. He tried to be a good Dixie drummer.
And Raymond Burke and Chester Craig on bass, and you and Gene Emott. Yeah, I remember what that was.
I got some acetates by that band. Yeah. They all moved to it though.
That fellow, who was the fellow? George Hartman, he was out there in the lake for a long time playing for the Thorngarals and all that.
This was at the Thorngarals. Frank Clark played a pretty good piano. Yeah, and this kid here was AJ Salaci. That was the last time I used him once and I was seeing old Gene and Bazley on the drum.
Oh, Lou Costello. Yeah. Lou Lou was playing the drum? Yeah, it says Lou on the drum. I'll get those Lou. Frank Clark on the piano. Clark Clark, yeah.
He used to tune piano. He was a professor in college and put it down there. There's Dick Allen right here.

Yeah, I can see Rawson Crawford's taking your picture. And in the picture up above that, Herbert Otto was recording. I made notes on that. Let's see. WNOE was broadcasting from the jazz club then. And I can see Lou Saino on trombone, you, Francis Murray, Tom Brown, and I can't see anybody else. Familiar faces.
This is as close as I've got to him. Yeah. You know what I'm talking about, huh? Yeah, I'll hurt.
Your advertisement is almost. He's on top, huh? Yeah. How do you like my slogan, huh?
Pile on border with sweetest music this side of heaven. Yeah. We used to use it.
Honest music this side of heaven.
